official_sources: HMLR Practice Guide 65 registration of mines and minerals
official_measurement_examples: mines and minerals can be registered separately from the surface estate
surface title can contain reservations or exclusions relating to mines and minerals
a mineral title does not automatically prove a right to enter or disturb the surface
mineral ownership is distinct from minerals planning permission
minerals safeguarding policy is distinct from mineral ownership
Coal Authority mining information is not a complete substitute for title evidence for all minerals
mineral-title status does not establish planning permission buildable area or final development yield
core_rules: surface ownership is not automatically mineral ownership
mineral title is not surface title
reservation must be read from title/deed evidence
mineral title does not automatically grant surface access
mineral ownership is not planning permission
planning permission is not mineral ownership
safeguarding area is not mineral title
Coal Authority data is not universal mineral-title evidence
title-plan surface geometry is not automatic vertical-right extent
separate registered mineral estate must retain title identity
mineral rights do not prove extraction consent
mineral rights do not prove development constraint outcome
mineral title does not establish utility capacity
mineral title does not calculate development yield
no parcel mineral-title clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official HM Land Registry, Coal Authority, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. PG65 update dated 1 June 2026 retained with surface/mineral/planning separation; no parcel promotion.
